workLog.step: Confirmed the defect against the code on main rather than against my own notes. Called count_upstream_refs from a copy of main's module on nine path shapes: four that should count returned 0, five that should not count returned 1.

Traced the cause. PR #3463 fixed a genuine mid-path defect by adding a bare lookbehind to the two templates patterns; the lookbehind also rejects the leading slash of an absolute path. The three legacy patterns were never touched and carry the mirror-image defect.

Replaced all five ad hoc prefixes with one shared boundary constant. The first revision consumed an optional leading separator and then applied a negative lookbehind, which admitted any character outside that set: ~/, C:\, ${ROOT}/, %ROOT%\, file:///, // and a #/ URL fragment all counted as repository-root references. Adversarial review caught it. The boundary now uses a positive start-of-context anchor that names the characters a path may follow.

Kept ../ excluded. An existing test asserts it. A parent-relative path does not unambiguously name the repository-root directory: where it lands depends on the referring file's own location, so it is not evidence of an upstream dependency. An earlier draft of the boundary allowed it and that test caught the regression.

Measured the change rather than asserting it. Loaded the module at 303f918ea and the branch module side by side and compared count_upstream_refs across 32 path shapes, then ran the branch test file against the module at 303f918ea: 22 of the 96 tests fail there, which is the behavior difference this branch encodes. Reproduce against 303f918ea, not against origin/main, because main has since absorbed this fix and reports 96 passed there.
Filed issue #3471 with the reproduction table before opening the PR.

Stripped fenced code that opens inside a blockquote. The anchor change made a GitHub admonition example count as prose. A close is only accepted in the context its open was found in, so a >-prefixed backtick line cannot end a top-level fence early.

Verified the reviewer's second finding before acting on it. Bare directory references that end at a word boundary are missed, but they return 0 at base commit 303f918ea as well, so the gap predates this branch. Filed as issue #3482 and left out of scope.

nextSteps: Issue #3465 tracks the unrelated gap that this validator only scans Markdown under .claude/skills, so shipped agents, rules, and instructions are not covered.
